REPO: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa
BRANCH: feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info (currently checked out, at develop's tip `8362b3c`)

THE SUBJECT is 29 staged-but-uncommitted files. List them with:
  git diff --cached --name-only
Read every one of them in full. They are the entire subject — nothing else on the branch differs from develop.

The feature is SFCC-89, "PDP static product information": rendering a product's name, price, description, style code and model line on the product detail page.

DOCUMENT under these headings, mirroring how a house standard would be organised. For each, state what the code does and cite `file:line`.

1. STYLING SURFACE — where styling lives for each component; recipe files and their shape; how they are registered; single-part vs multipart; how variants and state are expressed; token usage (`var(--zimm-*)`, bare keys, `textStyle`); any raw literals and how they are justified.
2. COMPONENT STRUCTURE — the atoms and molecule created, their folder layout, export style, prop types and placement, JSDoc.
3. DATA FLOW — where data is fetched, how it reaches the components, the page↔component boundary, any mapper or hook, how props cross composition boundaries.
4. MICROCOPY & CONTENT — how user-facing strings are sourced.
5. TESTING — every test and story file, what each asserts, how mocking is scoped, and which layer covers which behaviour.
6. STORYBOOK — story structure, titles, named exports, `play` usage, decorators.
7. ACCESSIBILITY — concrete practices in the code.
8. OVERRIDES — what is overridden and how; the copy-first port; import paths used and why; anything about the overrides resolver.
9. RICH TEXT / SANITISATION — how `utils/richText.tsx` works and why it exists rather than a library.

ALSO CAPTURE, verbatim from the code comments where present:
- The FOUR KNOWN OPEN ITEMS: (a) `c_modelFit` is not populated on any catalogue product checked, so the model line never renders; (b) the description renders both in the content group and in the base `InformationAccordion`, which reads the same `longDescription`; (c) translations were deliberately not modified (Tier 2); (d) hero layout metrics (218px column, 180px gap, 140px right margin, gallery ratio) were measured but not applied because they live inside `product-view`'s layout.
- THREE ALREADY-CLOSED CONFORMANCE GAPS, which you should VERIFY are genuinely closed rather than re-report as problems: (i) our four recipes are registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` alongside #59's twelve; (ii) `ZimmProductStyleCode` uses `useUiCopy` for its label rather than a prop; (iii) three component-level test files exist for the components with render branches. For each, state whether it is in fact closed, with `file:line`.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- READ-ONLY. Do not write, create or modify any file. Do not run mutating git commands (no checkout, stash, commit, add). Read-only git is fine.
- Every claim needs a `file:line`. Anything you cannot cite must be labelled "UNCITED — inference".
- Do not read anything under /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/ outside the repo.
- Report the code as it is, including anything that looks odd — but label observations as observations, not verdicts.

Return the implementation catalogue as your final report.

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe for the PDP `Content` group — the DS's own 218 x 82 frame holding name, price and
 * description. Not an invented grouping.
 *
 * The 20px rhythm is a flex `gap`, not a margin on each child. Two reasons:
 *
 *  - It collapses correctly when an optional field is absent. `ZimmProductDescription` returns
 *    `null` when the product has no description, so there is no second gap to suppress. A
 *    per-child `marginBottom` would need the parent to know which children rendered, and would
 *    leave a trailing gap when the last one did not.
 *  - It cannot be out-specified by a child. An adjacent-sibling rule (`& > * + *`) was tried
 *    first and silently lost to the `margin: 0` in `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` and
 *    `zimmProductDescription.css.ts` — equal specificity, and Emotion happened to inject the
 *    child classes last. `gap` is set on the container and no child declaration can reach it.
 *    The `play` in index.stories.tsx asserts the computed value so this cannot regress.
 */

/** DS: 20px between the name, price and description rows. Exactly `spacing.l`. */
const SPACE_WITHIN_TEXT_GROUP = 'var(--zimm-scale-l)'; // 20px

export const ZimmProductContent = {
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    flexDirection: 'column',
    alignItems: 'flex-start',
    gap: SPACE_WITHIN_TEXT_GROUP,
  } satisfies SystemStyleObject,
};

=== recipeGuards.test.ts scope/header ===
/**
 * Recipe guards — regression tests for four failure modes that reached a feature branch
 * despite passing `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit and the Storybook a11y run.
 *
 * All four share a shape: the value is a *valid* `SystemStyleObject` entry, so TypeScript is
 * satisfied; no lint rule covers it; and nothing asserts layout. Each one renders plausible,
 * wrong output that is only visible by opening the page.
 *
 *   1. A spacing-scale key on a sizing property. Chakra resolves `width`/`height`/`boxSize`
 *      through `theme.sizes`, not `theme.space`. The Zimmermann named scale is registered as
 *      `space` only (deliberately — see foundation/sizes.ts), so `width: 'xl'` silently reads
 *      Chakra's default `sizes.xl` = 36rem. It shipped a 576px icon and collapsed the footer.
 *
 *   2. The same trap on a typography property. `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are
 *      deliberately NOT registered either (theme/index.ts explains why), so a bare key reads
 *      Chakra's default or resolves to nothing at all. See TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS below.
 *
 *   3. A recipe key that collides with a base SFCC recipe. `theme/index.ts` composes with
 *      `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which DEEP MERGES — a recipe named `Footer` does
 *      not replace SFCC's `Footer`, it inherits it. Shared part names then pick up base
 *      properties, and a key you add that the base lacks is appended last, so a CSS shorthand
 *      can silently reset a longhand the base declared earlier.
 *
 *   4. A bare scale key inside a compound shorthand. Chakra resolves a token only when it is
 *      the entire value; `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim, the browser rejects the
 *      declaration, and the padding does not apply at all.
 *
 * A fifth guard below (`no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered
 * scale`) is a different kind of check — not a wrong-value bug, since `space` and `colors`
 * ARE registered Chakra scales (theme/index.ts), so a bare key there resolves to the correct
 * Zimmermann value either way. It enforces a house style instead: override components must
 * always reference a zimm value via `var(--zimm-scale-*)` / `var(--zimm-color-*)`, never a
 * bare Chakra token string, so a PR reviewer sees an unambiguous zimm reference at every call
 * site instead of having to recall which scales are and are not registered.
 *
 * SCOPE: these guards walk the registered recipe map only (`components` + the composed
 * `theme`). They cannot see the same mistakes made as a JSX prop on a component — there is a
 * live instance of failure mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302`
 * (`fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing) that no test here can reach. Catching that class needs
 * a static rule over JSX attributes (`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`), not a theme walk. The
 * house-style guard has the same JSX blind spot — `footerNavColumn/index.tsx` had a bare
 * `paddingLeft: '2xs'` in an inline `sx` merge (not a recipe) that this test cannot see;
 * it was only found by a manual grep across `overrides/app/components/`, not by this suite.

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
